events.title: Herostratus burns the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
events.description: Herostratus set fire to the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. The 6th-century BCE marble temple, partly paid for by King Croesus of Lydia, was rebuilt on an even larger scale.
events.html: Herostratus set fire to the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, one of the Seven Wonders of the ancient world. The 6th-century BCE marble temple, partly paid for by King Croesus of Lydia, was rebuilt on an even larger scale.

events.title: Alexander the Great is born in Pella
events.description: Alexander, son of Philip II of Macedon, was born by the traditional dating around 20 or 21 July. By his death at 32 he had conquered an empire stretching from Greece and Egypt to north-west India.

events.title: Berengar I has his rival Emperor Louis III blinded
events.description: Louis III, emperor and king of Italy, captured at Verona by his rival Berengar I, was blinded for breaking his oath and forced to give up both crowns. Remembered as Louis the Blind, he returned to rule Provence.

events.title: Louis IX defeats Henry III of England at Taillebourg
events.description: At the bridge over the Charente at Taillebourg, King Louis IX of France defeated Henry III of England and his stepfather Hugh X of Lusignan in the Saintonge War's decisive battle. The failure ended Henry's attempt to recover Poitou.
events.html: At the bridge over the Charente at Taillebourg, King Louis IX of France defeated Henry III of England and his stepfather Hugh X of Lusignan in the Saintonge War's decisive battle. The failure ended Henry's attempt to recover Poitou.

events.title: English ships first engage the Spanish Armada off Plymouth
events.description: The English fleet under Lord Howard and Drake attacked the Armada off Plymouth (21 July Old Style). The running fight up the Channel ended at Gravelines and in the Armada's disastrous voyage home.
events.html: The English fleet under Lord Howard and Drake attacked the Armada off Plymouth (21 July Old Style). The running fight up the Channel ended at Gravelines and in the Armada's disastrous voyage home.

events.title: Pope Clement XIV suppresses the Jesuits
events.description: Under pressure from the Catholic monarchies of France, Spain and Portugal, Clement XIV dissolved the Society of Jesus. The order survived in Russia and was restored worldwide in 1814.
events.html: Under pressure from the Catholic monarchies of France, Spain and Portugal, Clement XIV dissolved the Society of Jesus. The order survived in Russia and was restored worldwide in 1814.

events.title: Napoleon defeats the Mamluks at the Battle of the Pyramids
events.description: French infantry squares broke the charges of the Mamluk cavalry near Cairo. The victory gave Napoleon control of Egypt, where his expedition's scholars laid the foundations of modern Egyptology.
events.html: French infantry squares broke the charges of the Mamluk cavalry near Cairo. The victory gave Napoleon control of Egypt, where his expedition's scholars laid the foundations of modern Egyptology.

events.title: John Scopes is found guilty of teaching evolution
events.description: A Dayton jury convicted teacher John Scopes of breaking Tennessee's ban on teaching human evolution, and he was fined 100 dollars. The verdict was later overturned on a technicality.

events.title: Armstrong and Aldrin lift off from the Moon
events.description: After about 21 hours on the lunar surface, Armstrong and Aldrin fired the ascent stage of Eagle to rejoin Michael Collins in lunar orbit. They left a plaque reading 'We came in peace for all mankind'.
